The Pneuhage Group (Interpneu, Reifen Center Wolf, Gewe, with its own outlets, the Reifen1+ dealers and the First Stop franchise) and Reifen Göggel are the main independent wholesalers, with Best4Tires next, and are the fastest single-relationship route to volume. Michelin (Ihle, Euromaster), Continental (Vergölst), Hankook (Reifen Müller) and Goodyear (Reifen Burkhardt) already control their own downstream, so they are not viable access routes for a competing brand.

pc.note: Caveat The market, wholesale and direct figures are modelled from RecyBEM's 2024 placement of 9.99M tyres of all types, net of exports (checked), at an assumed 80% passenger cars. The flow model now also shows the gross layer: about 7.1M passenger-car tyres of pool sell-in, of which about 1.5M is re-exported by Dutch hubs. That is how a 9M Europool figure (consumer scope, 2026) fits an 8.0M domestic market. The flow model is 2024; the player volumes below are the research's 2026 basis (wholesale node 5.35M against 5.25M in 2024). No wholesaler or retailer publishes Dutch tyre volumes, so every player figure is a research estimate (outlets times an assumed throughput, or a share of the wholesale total) with low to medium confidence. Read the ranges and the ranking as indicative, not measured.
pc.marketAccessNote: Wholesale for passenger-car tyres is concentrated in one group. Global Automotive Investments Holding (Inter-Sprint, Van den Ban, Banden Express, PBG/Mega Tyre, Reedijk) is estimated by the research at about 60% of the Dutch wholesale node (2.9-3.6M tyres), so treat it as one key account; the remaining 1.5-2.2M sits with other wholesalers and importers. LKQ Fource and Alliance Automotive (Tyfoon) mostly resell tyres from Inter-Sprint to independent garages, so their volume is not additive. Sell-out is fragmented across a dense service network: Kwik Fit (165 outlets, planning to grow to 175), Profile (about 170), Euromaster (about 106 own and partner locations, owned by Michelin, about 65% commercial) and Bosch Car Service (about 400-415 workshops). Kwik Fit, Profile/Distri24 and the lease intermediaries are the largest buyers a brand can approach directly; Euromaster is Michelin-owned. Heuver is a major tyre group and Profile retailer, but its wholesale business is truck, agricultural and earthmoving, so it is not a passenger-car wholesale gateway.

The consumer total of 21.06M is the headline because MITECO's passenger-car line is not like-for-like with Europool's; the passenger-car-only cut (17.93M) is secondary. The Europool pool (14.775M, +2%) and the GfK channel shares are second-hand and not checked. Everything below the market figure (wholesale versus direct, channel shares, player volumes) is an estimate of low to medium confidence. Wholesalers publish revenue, not tyre units, so they are ranked on group revenue; retail volumes are derived from revenue and are indicative only.
pc.marketAccessNote: Spain is wholesaler-led: about 70% of consumer tyres (14.7M of 21.06M) pass through a wholesaler, and manufacturer-affiliated networks (Euromaster, First Stop, Vulco) are fed directly. Three groups are the main gateways: Grupo Soledad (EUR 409M group revenue in 2024, includes retail), Grupo Andrés (the largest pure, manufacturer-independent distributor, about EUR 360M from tyres) and NEX (EUR 290M; a 50/50 Euromaster/Rodi venture, so Michelin-linked, not independent). Soledad's Confortauto network is co-branded with Hankook and NEX is Michelin-linked, so for a challenger brand the cleanest routes are Andrés plus the manufacturer-neutral networks (Point S, and the autocentros Norauto, Feu Vert and Aurgi/Motortown). Dealers (about 2.0M tyres) buy through OEM parts programmes and wholesalers' dealer desks. Confortauto is Soledad's network, so it is counted once, inside Soledad.

pc.marketAccessNote: Italian wholesale is a few national groups plus a regional tier, not a two-name market. Fintyre Group (Fintyre, Franco Gomme and Gexpo Tyre; over 6M tyres a year across all categories) is the first anchor, followed by Univergomma, Gruppo Magri and Zuin, with Tagliabue Gomme Gross (TGG, €143.3M revenue in 2022) alongside them. TGG was acquired by Global Automotive Investments Holding BV in Dec 2023/Feb 2024, the same group that owns Van den Ban (already in your Netherlands list), a cross-border relationship worth exploring. Driver (Pirelli-owned, 400+ outlets) is the largest captive network and not an access route for a competing brand.

pc.marketAccessNote: Switzerland has no tyre production, so everything is imported, and the model puts about four in ten tyres on a direct route from the manufacturers. The largest chains are captive: BestDrive (Continental), Euromaster (Michelin), First Stop (Bridgestone) and Premio (Goodyear). The independent trade is served by ESA, the purchasing cooperative of the Swiss motor trade with about 7,000 co-owners, by Swiss Tyre Group (17 shareholders, 25 sales points), by a few small regional wholesalers and by cross-border supply from German wholesalers and online platforms. For Apollo the openings are ESA, Swiss Tyre Group, regional wholesalers and online, including its own reifen.com. Growth here depends on getting listed and priced competitively, not on finding an importer.
